questions.question:
Consider the operations
[latex]f(X,Y,Z)=X'YZ+XY'+Y'Z'[/latex] and [latex] g(X,Y,Z)=X'YZ+X'YZ'+XY[/latex].
Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation:
Post's theorem: a function alone is complete if it is not 0-preserving, not 1-preserving, not self-dual, not monotone and not linear.

f: f(0,0,0) = 1, f(1,1,1) = 0 (so also not monotone). f(0,0,1) = f(1,1,0) = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not self-dual. Not linear (fitting [latex]1\oplus Y\oplus Z[/latex] from the first rows gives f(1,1,1) = 1, but it is 0). So {f} is complete.

g: g(0,0,0) = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0-preserving, so {g} cannot produce 1 from 0s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not complete.

Answer: Only {f} is functionally complete

questions.question: Consider a uniprocessor system executing three tasks T1, T2 and T3, each of which is composed of an infinite sequence of jobs (or instances) which arrive periodically at intervals of 3, 7 and 20 milliseconds, respectively. The priority of each task is the inverse of its period, and the available tasks are scheduled in order of priority, with the highest priority task scheduled first. Each instance of T1, T2 and T3 requires an execution time of 1, 2 and 4 milliseconds, respectively. Given that all tasks initially arrive at the beginning of the 1st millisecond and task preemptions are allowed, the first instance of T3 completes its execution at the end of _____________ milliseconds.
questions.explanation:
Priorities: T1 (period 3) [latex]\gt[/latex] T2 (7) [latex]\gt[/latex] T3 (20).

- 0-1 T1, 1-3 T2, 3-4 T1 (new instance)
- 4-6 T3 (2 of 4 ms)
- 6-7 T1, 7-9 T2, 9-10 T1
- 10-12 T3 (remaining 2 ms) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] done

Answer: 12

questions.question: A positive edge-triggered D flip-flop is connected to a positive edge-triggered JK flip-flop as follows. The Q output of the D flip-flop is connected to both the J and K inputs of the JK flip-flop, while the Q output of the JK flip-flop is connected to the input of the D flip-flop. Initially, the output of the D flip-flop is set to logic one and the output of the JK flip-flop is cleared. Which one of the following is the bit sequence (including the initial state) generated at the Q output of the JK flip-flop when the flip-flops are connected to a free-running common clock? Assume that J=K=1 is the toggle mode and J=K=0 is the state-holding mode of the JK flip-flop. Both the flip-flops have non-zero propagation delays.
questions.explanation:
Each clock: J = K = old D output, and D takes the old JK output. Start D = 1, Q(JK) = 0.

- Clock 1: J=K=1, toggle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 1; D = 0
- Clock 2: J=K=0, hold [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 1; D = 1
- Clock 3: J=K=1, toggle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 0; D = 1
- Clock 4: toggle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 1; D = 0, and the pattern repeats

Sequence: 0 1 1 0 1 1 0...

Answer: 0110110...

questions.question: Consider a disk pack with a seek time of 4 milliseconds and rotational speed of 10000 rotations per minute (RPM). It has 600 sectors per track and each sector can store 512 bytes of data. Consider a file stored in the disk. The file contains 2000 sectors. Assume that every sector access necessitates a seek, and the average rotational latency for accessing each sector is half of the time for one complete rotation. The total time (in milliseconds) needed to read the entire file is ____________.
questions.explanation:
One rotation = 60 / 10000 s = 6 ms.

Per sector: seek 4 + latency 3 + transfer 6/600 = 0.01 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7.01 ms

Total = 2000 [latex]\times[/latex] 7.01 = 14020 ms

Answer: 14020

questions.question: Consider a non-pipelined processor with a clock rate of 2.5 gigahertz and average cycles per instruction of four. The same processor is upgraded to a pipelined processor with five stages; but due to the internal pipeline delay, the clock speed is reduced to 2 gigahertz. Assume that there are no stalls in the pipeline. The speed up achieved in this pipelined processor is_________.
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- Non-pipelined: 4 cycles / 2.5 GHz = 1.6 ns per instruction
- Pipelined (CPI 1): 1 / 2 GHz = 0.5 ns per instruction

Speed-up = 1.6 / 0.5 = 3.2

Answer: 3.2

questions.question: Suppose the following disk request sequence (track numbers) for a disk with 100 tracks is given: 45, 20, 90, 10, 50, 60, 80, 25, 70. Assume that the initial position of the R/W head is on track 50. The additional distance that will be traversed by the R/W head when the Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF) algorithm is used compared to the SCAN (Elevator) algorithm (assuming that SCAN algorithm moves towards 100 when it starts execution) is____________ tracks.
questions.explanation:
SSTF from 50: 50 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 45 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 60 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 70 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 80 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 90 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 20 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10
= 5 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 65 + 5 + 10 = 130

SCAN (elevator), going up and reversing after the last request: 50 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 90 = 40, then 90 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 = 80 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 120

Extra distance = 130 [latex]-[/latex] 120 = 10

questions.question: Consider a main memory with five page frames and the following sequence of page references: 3, 8, 2, 3, 9, 1, 6, 3, 8, 9, 3, 6, 2, 1, 3. Which one of the following is true with respect to page replacement policies First In First Out (FIFO) and Least Recently Used (LRU)?

options.A: Both incur the same number of page faults
options.B: FIFO incurs 2 more page faults than LRU
options.C: LRU incurs 2 more page faults than FIFO
options.D: FIFO incurs 1 more page faults than LRU

questions.explanation:
FIFO: 3, 8, 2, 9, 1 (5); 6 replaces 3; 3 replaces 8; 8 replaces 2; 2 replaces 9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 faults

LRU: 3, 8, 2, 9, 1 (5); 6 replaces 8; 8 replaces 2; 2 replaces 1; 1 replaces 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 faults

Answer: Both incur the same number of page faults

Consider the following 2x2 matrix A where two elements are unknown and are marked by a and b. The eigenvalues of this matrix are -1 and 7. What are the values of a and b?

- Trace: 1 + a = [latex]-[/latex]1 + 7 = 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a = 5

Answer: a = 5, b = 3

questions.question: An algorithm performs [latex](log N)^{1/2}[/latex] find operations, [latex]N[/latex]  insert operations, [latex](log N)^{1/2}[/latex] delete operations, and [latex](log N)^{1/2}[/latex] decrease-key operations on a set of data items with keys drawn from a linearly ordered set. For a delete operation, a pointer is provided to the record that must be deleted. For the decrease-key operation, a pointer is provided to the record that has its key decreased. Which one of the following data structures is the most suited for the algorithm to use, if the goal is to achieve the best total asymptotic complexity considering all the operations?
questions.explanation:
N inserts dominate. Compare total cost:

- Unsorted array: insert O(1), find O(N), delete/decrease-key with pointer O(1) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\sqrt{\log N})[/latex]
- Min-heap: N inserts cost [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- Sorted array / sorted list: each insert O(N) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Answer: Unsorted array

questions.question:
Consider the following pseudo code, where x and y are positive integers. 
 begin
   q := 0
    r := x 
    while r >= y  do
         begin
               r := r - y
              q := q + 1
        end
end
The post condition that needs to be satisfied after the program terminates is
questions.explanation:
The loop subtracts y from r and counts it in q, which is division of x by y. Invariant: x = qy + r. The loop stops when r [latex]\lt[/latex] y.

Answer: {x = qy + r [latex]\wedge[/latex] r [latex]\lt[/latex] y}

questions.question:
The probabilities that a student passes in mathematics, physics and chemistry are m,p and c respectively. Of these subjects, the student has 75% chance of passing in at least one, a 50% chance of passing in at least two and a 40% chance of passing in exactly two. Following relations are drawn in m,p,c:

I. p+m+c=27/20
II. p+m+c=13/20
III. (p)x(m)x(c)=1/10

options.C: Relations II and III are true.
options.D: Relations I and III are true.

questions.explanation:
P(exactly 3) = P(at least 2) [latex]-[/latex] P(exactly 2) = 0.5 [latex]-[/latex] 0.4 = 0.1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] pmc = 1/10 (III true).
P(exactly 1) = 0.75 [latex]-[/latex] 0.5 = 0.25

p + m + c = expected number of subjects passed = 1(0.25) + 2(0.4) + 3(0.1) = 1.35 = 27/20 (I true).

Answer: Relations I and III are true
